study_identification_part.si_4_title: Developmental trajectories of neuroanatomical alterations associated with the 16p11.2 Copy Number Variations

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: EU 16p11.2 consortium cohort; Simons VIP cohort; NIH MRI Study of Normal Brain Development (NIHPD) normative cohort.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "Cross-sectional data was acquired in 2 different cohorts (the European -EU 16p11.2 consortium and the Simons VIP -SVIP study in North America)"; "As normative reference data for brain growth, we used the multi-site longitudinal data from Objective 1 ... of the publicly available NIHPD project"
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.location: study_1/CardenasDeLaParra2019.pdf.md: 2.1.1. 16p11.2 CNVs cohort; 2.1.2. General population -NIHPD cohort

answer.EU: 16p11.2 cohort (DEL/DUP/CTRL) for clinical group comparison after normalization

answer.SVIP: 16p11.2 cohort (DEL/DUP/CTRL) for clinical group comparison after normalization

answer.NIHPD: normative reference dataset for age/sex modeling and Z-scoring

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: EU and SVIP provide deletion/duplication carriers and controls; NIHPD provides the normative developmental model used to compute Z-scores.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "Cross-sectional data was acquired in 2 different cohorts (the European -EU 16p11.2 consortium and the Simons VIP -SVIP study in North America)"; "As normative reference data for brain growth, we used the multi-site longitudinal data from Objective 1 ... of the publicly available NIHPD project"; "To compute Z-scores that normalize for the effect of growth and sex ... we modeled the effect of those 2 variables in the NIHPD normative dataset."
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: study_1/CardenasDeLaParra2019.pdf.md: 2.1.1. 16p11.2 CNVs cohort; 2.1.2. General population -NIHPD cohort; 2.4.1. Z-scoring for the main effect of age and gender for global and voxelbased volumes

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: NIHPD normative model used 339 children; total 874 longitudinal scans.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "The normative model (Aubert-Broche et al., 2011) used data from 339 children (179 females and 160 males), scanned longitudinally at 2 or 3 time points... for a total of 874 scans."
